value_stream.name: Corporate Real Estate & Property Portfolio Management

fields.Participants: Property Controller, Finance (links to VS-17), Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Treasury (links to VS-18)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "reporting and group consolidation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "review portfolio performance vs budget" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-134 (ensure property income & LGU tax compliance (as owner).)
- operational: capitalization policy (W3203/links to VS-35) and review; operational: automated IC matching (links to VS-17)
Pain Points / Risks: - **NOI-distortion risk**: Mis-classified capex vs opex inflates NOI; mitigated by capitalization policy (W3203/links to VS-35) and review
- **Intercompany-leak risk**: Incomplete elimination double-counts rent; mitigated by automated IC matching (links to VS-17.2/VS-72)
System Touchpoints: - Property accounting/GL (links to VS-17); consolidation (links to VS-17.2); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); valuation (links to W3189)

steps.activity: Property Controller close each property's P&L monthly: rental revenue (intercompany + third-party per W3195), CAM recovery net of recoverable expenses, other income (parking, signage), operating expenses (repairs/maintenance, utilities common area, security, property mgmt fee), property tax (W3202), insurance (W3204); compute NOI, cap rate on fair value (W3189), yield-on-cost

Finance (links to VS-17.4) consolidate property P&L into Property Mgmt Inc. entity reporting and group consolidation (links to VS-17.2); eliminate intercompany rent and intercompany profit on services; report NOI by property, by cluster, and portfolio

Director, Facilities & Real Estate/Finance review portfolio performance vs budget (links to VS-33) and prior year: occupancy, NOI growth, yield vs hurdle, variance drivers, watchlist properties; feed into strategy (W3185) and asset-plan decisions (hold/sell/redevelop — W3192)

fields.Participants: Property Tax Mgr, Finance (links to VS-79), Legal, LGU Assessor/Collector
fields.Trigger: Annual RPT cycle; LGU assessment notice; transfer of ownership (W3187)

workflows.name: Real Property Tax, Assessment & LGU Compliance (as Owner)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-reconcile of "reconcile to title/property master" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Pay annual RPT" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "Contest unfair assessments" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-134 (ensure property income & LGU tax compliance (as owner).)
- operational: master calendar and early-payment discipline; operational: systematic protest (LBAA) and appraisal evidence
Pain Points / Risks: - **Delinquency-auction risk**: Unpaid RPT can trigger LGU auction of the property; mitigated by master calendar and early-payment discipline
- **Over-assessment risk**: LGUs over-assess commercial property; mitigated by systematic protest (LBAA) and appraisal evidence
System Touchpoints: - Property tax module; tax compliance (links to VS-79); LGU compliance (links to VS-76); property master (links to VS-29)
Time Estimate: - 1–2 weeks/annual cycle per cluster; event-driven for protests

steps.activity: Property Tax Mgr maintain property tax declaration master: Tax Declaration No., classification (residential/commercial/industrial/ agricultural), assessed value, LGU/municipality, barangay, annual RPT due; reconcile to title/property master (links to VS-29/W3191) and to BuildRight-as-tenant RPT pass-through analysis (links to VS-42.3)

Pay annual RPT (on or before Jan 31, or quarterly per LGU schedule) to claim early-payment discount (typically 10–20%); for new acquisitions, transfer tax declaration to Property Mgmt Inc. name and update Assessor's Office; ensure no delinquency that could trigger auction/lien

Contest unfair assessments: file protest with Local Board of Assessment Appeals (LBAA) within statutory period where assessed value exceeds fair market value; document evidence (W3189 appraisal, sales comps); coordinate with VS-79 tax and VS-76 LGU compliance

fields.Participants: Property Dev Mgr, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Finance/Project Accounting (links to VS-40), Director, Facilities & Real Estate
fields.Trigger: Property condition assessment; tenant request; reserve study; lifecycle event

workflows.name: Capital Improvements, Repair Reserve & CAPEX Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Execute capital improvements per VS-40 project accounting" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-522 (ensure controlled execution — Property Accounting, Compliance & Portfolio Analytics (PA-97.3).)
- operational: reserve study and disciplined contribution; operational: capitalization policy (links to VS-35)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-reserving risk**: Insufficient reserves force deferred maintenance and emergency spend; mitigated by reserve study and disciplined contribution
- **Capitalization-error risk**: Operating repairs booked as capex inflate NOI/assets; mitigated by capitalization policy (links to VS-35)
System Touchpoints: - Reserve/funding (links to VS-18/VS-40); condition/CMMS (links to VS-20.3); project accounting (links to VS-40); fixed assets (links to VS-35)

steps.activity: Property Dev/Facilities maintain property condition assessments (links to VS-20.3 annual DC/store condition assessments): building systems (roof, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire, structural), parking/grounds, seismic/typhoon resilience (links to VS-69); estimate remaining useful life and replacement cost; build 5–10 year capital plan

Finance (links to VS-40) fund a repair/replacement reserve per reserve study: set reserve contribution per property from NOI, segregate funds, project cash needs vs reserves; governance for reserve draw (board authority per VS-36)

Execute capital improvements per VS-40 project accounting: scope/bid/build (links to VS-20.2), track cost and schedule, capitalize qualifying expenditures to investment property (W3188/W3189), activate; ensure LGU permits (links to VS-22/VS-76) and tenant coordination (W3196)

fields.Participants: Risk & Insurance Mgr, Treasury/Finance (links to VS-18/VS-26), Legal, Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Insurer/Broker
fields.Trigger: Annual renewal; acquisition (W3187); significant change/loss event

workflows.name: Property Insurance, Risk Transfer & Coverage Program

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "file and compliant" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-allocate of "allocate premium and claim recoveries to property-level P&L" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-522 (ensure controlled execution — Property Accounting, Compliance & Portfolio Analytics (PA-97.3).)
- operational: appraisal-based limits and BI/loss-of-rent coverage; operational: compliance monitoring (W3196) and landlord-purchased coverage
Pain Points / Risks: - **Underinsurance risk**: Typhoon/seismic losses exceed limits/sub-limits; mitigated by appraisal-based limits and BI/loss-of-rent coverage
- **Uninsured-gap risk**: Tenant-provided lapsed certificates expose landlord; mitigated by compliance monitoring (W3196) and landlord-purchased coverage
System Touchpoints: - Insurance register/claims (links to VS-26); GL/allocation (links to VS-17); risk register (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Risk & Insurance Mgr design portfolio insurance program: property/all-risk (fire, typhoon, flood, earthquake — critical for PH per VS-69), business interruption / loss of rent (for lessor income protection), boiler & machinery, general liability, builder's risk during construction (W3188); coverage limits, deductibles, sub-limits, per-location scheduling

Broker/Insurer place coverage: market the program to insurers, negotiate premium and terms, bind policies; confirm Property Mgmt Inc./Holdings as named insured, lender as loss-payee where financed (W3190), tenants per lease requirements; ensure tenant-provided insurance certificates on file and compliant (W3196)

Finance (links to VS-26.3) manage claims and premium allocation: allocate premium and claim recoveries to property-level P&L (W3201); manage claim filing, adjuster coordination, and recovery for typhoon/seismic events (links to VS-26/VS-69); maintain insurance register

fields.Participants: Property Mgr, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Janitorial/Security (links to VS-98), Landscaping Vendor, Store Ops (links to VS-07)
fields.Trigger: Daily operations; scheduled maintenance; tenant service (W3196)
fields.Volume: ~205+ properties with common areas, parking, grounds

workflows.name: Common Area, Grounds & Facility Operations Oversight

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedule preventive maintenance via CMMS" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-inspect of "manage service vendors" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "logbook and inspection records" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-522 (ensure controlled execution — Property Accounting, Compliance & Portfolio Analytics (PA-97.3).)
- operational: inspection and preventive maintenance; operational: lease definitions and transparent CAM ledger (W3195)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Safety-liability risk**: Slips/falls, inadequate lighting, drainage failures create liability; mitigated by inspection and preventive maintenance
- **Cost-allocation disputes**: CAM-recoverable vs landlord cost disputes; mitigated by lease definitions and transparent CAM ledger (W3195)
System Touchpoints: - CMMS/CAFM (links to VS-20.3); vendor mgmt (links to VS-34/VS-98); CAM allocation (links to W3195)

steps.activity: Property Mgr/Facilities operate common areas: parking lot maintenance (line marking, lighting, drainage — critical in PH rainy season), landscaping, signage, exterior lighting, waste collection (links to VS-73); schedule preventive maintenance via CMMS (links to VS-20.3)

Property Mgr manage service vendors: security (links to VS-98 contingent workforce), janitorial (links to VS-98), landscaping, pest control, fire-life-safety inspections; SLA and invoice validation (links to VS-15/VS-34); allocate vendor cost to CAM recoverable vs landlord-responsibility for billing (W3195)

Property Mgr coordinate with Store Ops (links to VS-07) for shared facility operations (loading dock, customer entrance, utilities) and with tenants (W3196); maintain property logbook and inspection records; feed issues to capital plan (W3203)

fields.Participants: Property Compliance Mgr, Legal, Environmental (links to VS-24/VS-73/VS-25), Director, Facilities & Real Estate, LGU/DENR

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify zoning and land-use compliance for each property" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitoring" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document compliance, correct violations within cure period, appeal where…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-522 (ensure controlled execution — Property Accounting, Compliance & Portfolio Analytics (PA-97.3).)
- operational: compliance register and variances; operational: W3191 ESA and remediation reserves
Pain Points / Risks: - **Use-nonconformity risk**: Operating outside zoning invites LGU shutdown/penalty; mitigated by compliance register and variances
- **Environmental-liability risk**: Undisclosed contamination transfers to owner; mitigated by W3191 ESA and remediation reserves
System Touchpoints: - Compliance register (links to VS-22/VS-76); environmental (links to VS-24/VS-25/VS-73); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Property Compliance Mgr/Legal verify zoning and land-use compliance for each property: LGU comprehensive land-use plan (CLUP) conformity (commercial use), building height/density/setback compliance, environmental compliance certificate (ECC) where required (DENR), tree-cutting permits, water/discharge permits; maintain compliance register per property

Environmental (links to VS-25.1/VS-73.2) manage environmental obligations: hazardous-materials disclosure (asbestos/lead in older structures, paint/chemical storage per VS-24.3), soil/groundwater if contaminated site (links to W3191 Phase II), waste-water and air-quality permits; coordinate VS-73 hazardous-waste and VS-25 ESG monitoring

Respond to LGU/DENR inspections and notices (links to VS-22.2/VS-76): document compliance, correct violations within cure period, appeal where warranted; manage zoning/variance applications for repositioning/redevelopment (links to W3188)

fields.Participants: Transfer Pricing Mgr, Tax (links to VS-79), Finance (links to VS-72), Director, Facilities & Real Estate, External TP Advisor
fields.Trigger: Annual TP cycle (links to VS-72); new intercompany lease (W3193); renewal (W3197)
fields.Volume: ~50 intercompany leases (the owned-site portfolio per W119; the ~205 total lease portfolio is predominantly third-party per W1183)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "methodology per BIR RR 02-2013 and OECD guidelines" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document in TP documentation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "Defend on BIR audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-522 (ensure controlled execution — Property Accounting, Compliance & Portfolio Analytics (PA-97.3).)
- operational: CUP benchmarking and contemporaneous docs; operational: single source of truth per property
Pain Points / Risks: - **TP-adjustment risk**: BIR challenges intercompany rent as non-arm's-length; mitigated by CUP benchmarking and contemporaneous docs
- **Inconsistency risk**: Rent, RPT basis, and valuation inputs must reconcile; mitigated by single source of truth per property
System Touchpoints: - TP documentation (links to VS-72); tax (links to VS-79); billing (W3195); valuation (W3189)

steps.activity: Transfer Pricing Mgr/TP Advisor conduct annual arm's-length benchmarking for intercompany rent: comparable uncontrolled price (CUP) using third-party lease comps (W3194 market deals) and market data, build per-sqm market rent range by location class (NCR/Visayas/Mindanao, mall vs standalone, store format); document methodology per BIR RR 02-2013 and OECD guidelines

Compare intercompany rent charged (W3193/W3195) to arm's-length range; adjust where outside range; document in TP documentation (master file, local file, country-by-country where applicable); ensure consistency between rent charged, RPT basis (W3202), and valuation inputs (W3189)

Defend on BIR audit (links to VS-79.3/VS-22.2): produce TP documentation, benchmarking, comparables, and contemporaneous evidence; manage any BIR adjustment, interest, and penalty; update framework (W3193)

fields.Participants: Director, Facilities & Real Estate, Finance (links to VS-17), Valuation (links to W3189), ESG/Sustainability (links to VS-25), Strategy (links to VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Quarterly portfolio review; annual reporting; board/investor reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-collect of "collection, cap rate movement vs W3189 fair value, debt metrics" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "report portfolio valuation roll-forward" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-register of "Director, Facilities & Real Estate/Strategy present to Board" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-522 (ensure controlled execution — Property Accounting, Compliance & Portfolio Analytics (PA-97.3).)
- operational: BI automation (links to VS-28) and monthly close discipline (W3201); operational: auditable metrics
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reporting-lag risk**: Stale portfolio data delays decisions; mitigated by BI automation (links to VS-28) and monthly close discipline (W3201)
- **Greenwashing risk**: Overstating ESG performance attracts scrutiny (links to VS-25); mitigated by auditable metrics
System Touchpoints: - Portfolio analytics/BI (links to VS-28); valuation (W3189); ESG (links to VS-25); board reporting (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Finance/Director, Facilities & Real Estate produce portfolio performance pack: NOI by property/cluster/region, occupancy, WAL (weighted-average lease term), collection, cap rate movement vs W3189 fair value, debt metrics (W3190), capex vs reserve (W3203), watchlist; benchmark to budget (links to VS-33) and market
steps.r: Finance Analyst / Director, Facilities & Real Estate

steps.activity: Valuation/ESG (links to VS-25/W3189) report portfolio valuation roll-forward: opening fair value, additions (W3187/W3188), disposals (W3192), fair-value movement, transfers, closing fair value; ESG metrics — green-building certifications (links to VS-78), energy/carbon (links to VS-25.1/W1563), climate-risk exposure (typhoon/seismic per VS-69), social/community impact

Director, Facilities & Real Estate/Strategy present to Board (links to VS-36.1) and Holdings: portfolio strategy execution, key deals, risk register (links to VS-21.2), outlook; integrate findings into next-strategic-cycle (W3185) and group consolidation/disclosure (links to VS-17.2/VS-17.4)
